questions.q: The most important part of communication is often…
options: Listening to understand, not just to reply
questions.explain: Listening to understand is what makes the other person feel heard — and reveals what to say next.

questions.q: To make an email clear, you should…
options: Bury the ask at the end
Lead with the key point and the action needed
questions.explain: Busy readers skim. Put the point and the ask up front.

options: Planning your reply while they talk
Paraphrasing back to confirm you understood
questions.explain: Reflecting back what you heard confirms understanding and shows you were truly listening.

questions.q: When giving difficult feedback, tone should be…
questions.explain: Calm and specific lets the message land without triggering defensiveness.

options: The words, detail and examples you choose
questions.explain: The same idea is framed differently for an exec, a peer, or a beginner.

questions.q: A good way to check you were understood is to…
options: Ask them to summarise the next step
questions.explain: Having them restate the action confirms the message actually landed.
